chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the slave girl whose master dies. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She observes the waiting period of the one widowed from her husband.' I said: 'If a man marries her before her waiting period ends?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He separates from her, then he marries her with a new marriage after the completion of her waiting period.' I said: 'So where is what has reached us from your father (peace be upon him) regarding the man who marries the woman during her waiting period, that she does not become permissible for him forever?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is an ignorant (person).'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a slave girl when her master dies and how is her marriage affected if contracted early?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that an umm al-walad observes the iddah of a widow upon her master's death, establishing the procedure for remarriage if contracted prematurely. He refutes the notion of permanent invalidity by attributing it to a narrator's ignorance, thereby distinguishing between a temporary defect in the marriage contract and a permanent prohibition. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of marital contracts and the critical role of narrator reliability in deriving legal precedents.
